current.text: He is out with plantar fasciitis and a toe issue in his foot. The injury is expected to keep him out at least four weeks.
Because of the foot injury, experts no longer want him as a late-round pick or a starter-level flyer.
He re-signed with Utah for 2 years and 22 million USD. Walker Kessler is no longer on the team, which leaves the starting center job open.
Jaxson Hayes started at center in the preseason because Utah does not want Jaren Jackson Jr. playing much center. Kyle Filipowski is back in the rotation.
When healthy, experts expect him to be Utah's starting center, though not all are sure he wins the job over Ace Bailey.
He was about a top 70 player last season and played very well as a starter after Kessler got hurt.
If he starts, one expert expects at least top 80 numbers.
His passing should matter more in Utah because Jaren Jackson Jr. and Kyle Lowry are not good passers.
Utah plans to win this season, not tank, so experts see little risk of late-season shutdowns or cut minutes.

durable.text: He has a long history of knee, leg and other lower-body injuries. Experts do not see him as a reliable or healthy player.
He rebounds well, passes well for a center and protects the rim.
He is not a high-usage player.
His FT% is a clear weakness, even for a center, so he fits punt FT% builds.

note: Before his foot injury he was a popular late-round value pick. Now he is ranked 115 on Yahoo (2 USD) and 170 on ESPN (0 USD), and he went undrafted in our league last season. He is out at least four weeks, and experts have dropped him as a late-round target, so let him go undrafted in our 144-player auction. Watch two things early on waivers: when he gets back, and whether Jaxson Hayes keeps the starting center job. As a starter he can return about top 80 value for punt FT% builds that want rebounds and passing from a center.
